supersedes_note: Version 3 governs the W3 board. rubric.v2.md is not edited, not moved and not relocked; tools/verify.mjs recomputes both digests on every run, and the W2 rubric against its own lock, so a changed gate has to be a new version rather than an edit.

ordering_evidence.observed: rubric.v3.md was written AFTER the v2 board was rendered, by an independent Claude design-primary audit of those renders.
ordering_evidence.what_can_be_said_instead: A statement about method, not about priority. A7 and A8 were derived from defects already found in the rendered board and then implemented as machine checks rather than fitted to a wanted result: A7 fails ten of the eighty-one existing renders and A8 failed the registry as it stood. No render was redrawn to satisfy either.
ordering_evidence.honest_scope: The pre-registration claim in this study belongs to rubric.v2.md, and — more weakly, and disproved for two of a-critical-path-and-room's fields — to registry.json. See rubric.v3.md, 'What the ordering evidence is worth'.

rule: tools/verify.mjs recomputes the digest of rubric.v3.md on every run and fails if it differs. Changing a gate means adding a new versioned rubric and a new lock, never editing these bytes in place.
